**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Emit the process summary once**

In apps or tests that create more than one r300 context in a process, this destructor hook runs once per context while `counters` is a single process-wide static, so later teardowns re-emit the cells already reported by earlier teardowns. **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Replace failed retained files before dedupe**

When a write or `fclose` fails after creating `<dir>/r2vb-vs-...`, the code increments `retain_failures` but leaves the partial file behind. On the next occurrence of the same shader, this existence check treats that corrupt or empty file as a completed retention and returns, so a transient ENOSPC or interrupted write permanently loses that producer from the retained corpus until the directory is manually cleaned; write to a temporary file and rename, or unlink on failure.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Treat zero-valued retention gate as closed**

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Record structural rejects in production telemetry**

For `R300_R2VB_RESTAGE` workloads where the bound VS has control flow, unsupported intrinsics, or another structural reject, `r300_vs_is_fragment_aluable()` returns false before it calls `r300_r2vb_producer_fits_budget()`, so this shadow-check hook is never reached and the new `by_reason` counters never record those real reject classes. Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use unique temp names for concurrent retention**

When two r300 contexts in the same process first retain the same shader concurrently, both publishers use the same `<final>.tmp.<pid>` path; one `open(O_EXCL)` loses with `EEXIST` and increments `retain_failures`, and if the winning writer later fails the specimen is lost even though another writer could have completed it. **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use location rank for the computed-varying first input**

In cv=1 shaders whose NIR input variable list is not sorted by attribute location, this selects the declaration-list head as the only input allowed to feed computation. Rank `first_in` by input location here to match the actual producer/re-ingest wiring.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Drop varying-only ops before cv=0 scans**

For cv=0 shaders where `gl_Position` restages cleanly but a non-position output contains typed or otherwise unsupported work, this only skips the varying-store discipline; the earlier whole-shader structure scan and the later `plan_scan_typed_source()` still inspect the varying-only instructions. **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject strides beyond the LOAD_VBPNTR byte field**

When the application vertex buffer uses a stride greater than 1020 bytes, this initializer still returns success and stores `src_stride_bytes / 4` for later packet emission. The `3D_LOAD_VBPNTR` format word only has one byte for the dword stride (`r300_reg.h` describes the stride as the high byte, and `R300_VBPNTR_STRIDE*` shifts bytes/4 into that byte), so accepting values above `0xff` will either overlap the adjacent size/stride field or truncate to zero when the slot-fetch path emits the packet. Please fail the contract when `src_stride_bytes / 4 > 0xff`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include the 16-byte fetch in the offset overflow check**

When `buffer_offset + src_offset + start * src_stride_bytes` lands in the last 15 bytes of the uint32 offset range, this returns success even though stream 1 always advertises a 4-dword `R32G32B32A32_FLOAT` fetch. The packet can encode the starting offset, but the element itself spans past the representable byte range, so the BO-fetched producer path can wrap or read outside the intended buffer instead of falling back; please include the 16-byte element size in the overflow check.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Ground the GA-stall claim in evidence**

`AGENTS.md` says hardware/root-cause claims come from primary sources and code comments must distinguish known, hypothesized, and speculative claims, but this new source comment states the GA front-end stall mechanism as fact without naming the silicon observation, spec, kernel source, or retained evidence behind it. For this hardware-facing contract, the next reader cannot tell whether the tuple rule is measured RS482 behavior or a suspected cause, so attach the named evidence/source or mark the stall mechanism as a hypothesis.

**issue (bug_risk):** Guard against NULL `out` to avoid undefined behavior.

Only `s` is validated; `out` is assumed non-NULL. If a caller passes NULL for `out`, `out->streams = *s;` will dereference it and trigger UB. Either add a defensive `if (!out) return false;` or assert/document that `out` must be non-NULL as part of the API contract.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Record input facts per vertex state**

When telemetry is enabled with routing disabled, this new `r2vb_producer_input` record is emitted only while the shader/space memo is still `R300_R2VB_ADMIT_UNMEASURED`; after the first candidate draw sets that memo to reject, the same VS can be rebound with a different `src_format`, stride, draw start, or resource width and no new input record is printed. Those are exactly the facts the BO-fetch admission depends on, so retained experiments can learn the fetch envelope from whichever draw happened first rather than from all vertex-buffer states used by that shader.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Record every producer input**

For candidate shaders whose position producer reads multiple model attributes, this telemetry still hard-codes `velem[0]` and prints only `input=0`, while the producer path in this file can read `velem[0..num_in-1]`. In that scenario the retained BO-fetch data has no format/stride/extent facts for the secondary inputs, so the next fetch-contract widening can be calibrated against an incomplete input envelope.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Report aligned vertex-format dwords**

For vertex formats whose block size is not a multiple of four bytes, this records `format_dwords=0` or otherwise truncates because it divides the raw block size by 4. The direct-VB setup derives fetch dwords from `align(util_format_get_blocksize(...), 4) / 4`, so this telemetry understates the LOAD_VBPNTR size for the non-FP32 formats that the observation path is supposed to classify next.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Release the saved buffer on all failure paths**

This branch now returns the old upload buffer through `*releasebuf` on allocation failure, but several direct callers still exit before releasing it. For example, `primconvert_init_draw` returns false after `u_upload_alloc` fails and `util_primconvert_draw_single_vbo` returns at `src/gallium/auxiliary/indices/u_primconvert.c:294-295`, before the only `pipe_resource_release` at line 298; `u_vbuf_upload_buffers` similarly returns at `src/gallium/auxiliary/util/u_vbuf.c:1169-1170` or `1233-1234` without publishing `release_count`. In those OOM/fault-injection paths the handed-back buffer is still leaked, so this API change needs the callers' failure cleanup updated or the helper must retain the old clearing behavior for callers that do not opt in.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Clear stale outbufs on allocation failure**

When reallocation fails after a previous successful upload, callers that pass persistent output storage can still contain the old buffer because this failure path sets `*ptr` and `*out_offset` but leaves `*outbuf` untouched. In the `u_vbuf_upload_buffers` user-buffer path, `real_vb->buffer.resource` can therefore remain non-NULL from the prior draw, so the `if (!real_vb->buffer.resource)` check at `src/gallium/auxiliary/util/u_vbuf.c:1169` misses the allocation failure, proceeds with `buffer_offset == ~0`, and later releases the same old buffer returned through `releasebufs`; clearing `*outbuf` on this path makes the new hand-back semantics observable to these callers.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Match position-source ranks to the restage ordering**

For VS inputs that share `data.location` but differ by `location_frac` or declaration order, this scan gives them the same rank because it counts only strictly smaller locations. The restaged producer maps inputs with a total order of location, fraction, then list index, so a position input in a later fraction can be recorded as rank 0 even though the producer reads it from `VAR1`; when `position_source` is consumed, the BO-fetch binding can accept and fetch the wrong vertex element for component-split attributes.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include the RS TEX_PTR in the TC0 route check**

When `ip[0]` carries a stale nonzero `R300_RS_TEX_PTR`, this predicate still succeeds because it masks only the component selectors and the count. That pointer is in the same RS_IP word and selects which VAP texcoord components TC0 reads, so a block can pass the contract while routing TC0 from the wrong or out-of-range VAP component even though S/T/R/Q are C0..C3.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Verify the RS instruction selects IP0**

If `inst[0]` has `R300_RS_INST_TEX_ID(1)` while the write bit and destination address match, this helper returns true even though the instruction selects a different RS_IP entry than the one validated by `r2vb_rs_tc0_components_ok`. A stale TEX_ID can therefore pass the binding check while sourcing the FS input from another IP slot.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject stale PSC control bits**

A PSC element with the expected data type but stale `R300_SKIP_DWORDS` bits still passes here because only the low data-type nibble, destination, and LAST_VEC are checked. In the BO-fetch producer that changes how the VAP advances through the source record, so the checker can return zero for a transaction that fetches the wrong bytes; the control word needs to prove the unused control bits are clear as well.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Pin the binding to the POS/TC0 vector locations**

When a caller passes noncanonical destination vectors, this only rejects aliasing even though the RS block being validated is the fixed POS + TC0 tuple: POS is vector 0 and the first generic TC0 is vector 6 in the r300 stream layout. `r300_r2vb_producer_binding_check()` then validates the PSC against those same wrong binding values, so a transaction with `slot_dst_vec_loc=1` or `model_dst_vec_loc=7` can report zero violations while the rasterizer reads stale vector 0/TC0 data.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject extra RS instructions that overwrite the input**

When `rs->inst_count` names more than instruction 0, the emitter sends every RS instruction, but this check validates only `inst[0]`. A stale later instruction that also writes `binding->fs_hw_input_reg` can overwrite the producer model input after the validated TC0 write while the binding checker still returns zero, so the contract needs to require the single-instruction RS block or validate the RS tail.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject GB stuffing state in the RS binding**

When the prior draw leaves point-sprite stuffing bits in `rs->gb_enable`, this constructor still accepts the RS block because the validator list never checks that emitted register. `r300_emit_rs_block_state()` sends `gb_enable` with the RS block and `r300_state_derived.c` sets `R300_GB_POINT_STUFF_ENABLE`/`R300_GB_TEX*_SOURCE` for sprite-coordinate paths, so the producer's point draw can have TC0 stuffed by GB state instead of routed from the validated VAP vector while the binding check reports success.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Propagate source-scan allocation failures**

If `r300_r2vb_position_source_scan()` fails its clone allocation here, the failure is ignored and the plan can still be cached as a stable READY plan with `position_source.valid == false`. That turns a transient memory-pressure failure into a persistent BO-fetch decline for this VS until the shader is destroyed, instead of following the surrounding plan contract that allocation failures return `TRANSIENT_FAILURE` and are not cached.

When this READY transaction is emitted in the same CS and the following normal/re-ingest draw has the same cached vertex-array tuple, `r300_prepare_for_rendering` can skip `r300_emit_vertex_arrays` because it only checks `vertex_arrays_dirty/indexed/offset/instance_id` in `r300_render.c:265-269`. This custom `LOAD_VBPNTR` has just rebound the hardware to the producer slot/model BOs, but the context cache is left saying the application arrays are still current, so the next draw can fetch from the producer BOs unless this path marks the vertex arrays dirty after emission.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Re-reserve CS space after a validation flush**

When the first `cs_validate` in staging fails on a real winsys, the flush path can re-arm all atoms dirty (`r300_rearm_after_hardware_flush`), but staging retries validation and transitions to READY without running the capacity reservation again. In that case this call emits the enlarged dirty-state set even though `r300_r2vb_reserve_bo_draw_cs` only accounted for the smaller pre-flush dirty set, so a validation retry can overflow the IB or trip the per-atom `BEGIN_CS` assertions before the fixed producer range is emitted.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Force one-pixel points for the producer draw**

When the application rasterizer has a non-1 point size or point-size min/max state, `r300_emit_dirty_state` restores that GA point state immediately before this producer `PRIM_POINTS` draw. Because the producer maps vertex `i` to texel `(i, 0)` in a one-row FP32x4 render target, inheriting a wide point splats each slot over multiple texels and corrupts the BO-fetch output; the producer path needs to emit the same fixed 1-pixel `GA_POINT_SIZE`/`GA_POINT_MINMAX` override before drawing.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bypass app clip and viewport state for slot points**

When the bound application state uses clip-space VTE or clipping/scissor that excludes the first row, `r300_emit_dirty_state` leaves those registers live for this producer draw. The slot BO is a window-space point stream (`slot + 0.5, 0.5`), and the existing immediate producer emits `R300_CLIP_DISABLE` plus `R300_VTX_XY_FMT | R300_VTX_Z_FMT` before its point draw; without equivalent overrides here, the producer points can be transformed or clipped before they write the output row.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Redirty app PSC/RS after the producer draw**

After this custom producer emits its own PSC and RS/VAP register snapshots, the context still records the application `vertex_stream_state` and `rs_block_state` atoms as clean because `r300_emit_dirty_state` just cleared them. A later normal or fallback draw in the same context can therefore skip re-emitting the application PSC/RS state and run with the producer's stream layout and RS program; mark those owners dirty (or restore them) when the transaction reaches EMITTED.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve the caller's pending CS before capture**

When `R300_R2VB_SLOT_FETCH=1` and `R300_R2VB_BO_DRAW=capture` are set, this call runs from `r300_flush` while the caller's current command stream may already contain the draw being flushed. The helper then calls `cs_flush(..., RADEON_FLUSH_NOOP, NULL)`, which takes the winsys no-submit path and resets the current CS, so falling through here can create a fence for only cleanup/empty work while the original draw never reaches `DRM_RADEON_CS`. The capture path needs to avoid consuming the caller's pending CS, or return/restore/re-emit it before normal flushing.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep framebuffer surfaces consistent during capture**

When the gate is enabled while the framebuffer atom is still dirty (for example, a frontend binds an FBO and flushes before the next draw), staging calls `r300_add_state_buffers` with `r300->fb_state.state` pointing at this synthetic `pipe_framebuffer_state`. That path reads `fb->cbufs[0].texture` from `cap_fb` but still dereferences `r300->fb_cbufs[0]` for the domain, so a context with no installed cbuf surface can crash, and one with an old surface validates the new BO using the old surface's domain. The capture should either install a matching surface through the normal framebuffer setter or avoid swapping `fb_state.state` while dirty validation can run.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject user vertex buffers before BO-fetch setup**

When `R300_R2VB_BO_DRAW=producer_capture3` or `producer_submit3` is armed on a draw whose position element is backed by a Gallium user vertex buffer, this check reads the `pipe_vertex_buffer` union through the `resource` arm even though `is_user_buffer` selects `buffer.user` (`src/gallium/include/pipe/p_state.h` lines 632-640). A non-NULL user pointer passes here, and the next setup dereferences it as `vb->buffer.resource->width0`, so the diagnostic path can crash or read arbitrary user vertex bytes as a `pipe_resource` instead of declining cleanly. Check `vb->is_user_buffer` before using `buffer.resource`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Re-dirty all state after the no-submit capture**

When `R300_R2VB_BO_DRAW=producer_capture3` succeeds, the path has already run `r300_r2vb_prepare_states`, which emits and clears the current dirty atoms, and then discards that command stream with `RADEON_FLUSH_NOOP` without going through `r300_flush`'s full rearm. This line only re-dirties the raster subset, so a fallback draw after a captured producer can skip non-raster state that was emitted into the discarded IB, such as blend, textures, or other clean-again atoms, and render with stale hardware state. Re-dirty the full emitted state set after the no-submit flush before returning to gallivm.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Decline BO-fetch after model-list rewrites**

When the BO-fetch arm is combined with a path that has already rewritten `model` into a CPU-generated list, such as `R300_R2VB_TOPOLOGY` on an indexed triangle that gathers to three vertices, this call still passes the original `draw->start`. The new transaction ignores the gathered/clipped `model` array and materializes from the bound application vertex buffer at that start, so `producer_capture3`/`producer_submit3` can test different vertices than the draw being routed. Decline this arm after a model-list rewrite, or feed it the rewritten rows.

`Mesa NIR nir_intrinsic_load_ubo_uniform_block intrinsic definition`

💡 Result:

There is no standard Mesa NIR intrinsic defined as nir_intrinsic_load_ubo_uniform_block. The primary NIR intrinsic for accessing Uniform Buffer Objects is nir_intrinsic_load_ubo [1][2][3]. In Mesa's NIR (New Intermediate Representation), intrinsics are used to represent operations that interact with memory, variables, or system-provided values [4]. The nir_intrinsic_load_ubo intrinsic is specifically used for reading data from UBOs [1][2]. It typically takes the UBO index and a byte offset as sources [3]. The term uniform block generally refers to the GLSL concept of a uniform buffer object, and while NIR has lowering passes such as nir_lower_uniforms_to_ubo to manage the mapping of uniforms to UBOs [5][6], it does not utilize a distinct load_ubo_uniform_block intrinsic to perform these loads. The definition and management of all available NIR intrinsics are contained within the src/compiler/nir/nir_intrinsics.py file in the Mesa source tree [7][8].

**suggestion (bug_risk):** Guard against NULL `why` when emitting decline telemetry

The decline path assumes `why` is always set whenever `supported` becomes false. While current cases do this, any future path that sets `supported = false` without also setting `why` will pass a NULL pointer to `%s`, which is undefined behavior. For the native ICD, `r3v_physical_device.c` still advertises `VK_KHR_swapchain` and initializes common WSI, and the existing Gallium device dispatch adds `wsi_device_entrypoints`; this new native dispatch table only layers `r3v_device_entrypoints` and `vk_common_device_entrypoints`. Because the native physical device inherits `VK_KHR_dedicated_allocation`, callers may chain `VkMemoryDedicatedRequirements` through `vkGetBufferMemoryRequirements2` or `vkGetDeviceBufferMemoryRequirements`; the Gallium R3V buffer path explicitly writes both booleans false for buffers, but this native path only overwrites `memoryRequirements` and leaves the pNext struct untouched.
